articles.title: The funniest man you know is directing the twistiest, darkest movie of the year
articles.summary: "Verity" director Michael Showalter’s career began on MTV’s early '90s cult sketch-comedy show “The State.” Thirty years later, he’s helming big Hollywood fi...
articles.body:
At the U.K. premiere of Verity in London last month, director Michael Showalter said it was a " lifelong dream " to make an erotic psychological thriller.

"It's a dream come true for me to direct a film like this," Showalter said on the red carpet. "I've always loved the thriller, the erotic thriller, the psychological thriller."

That may sound strange coming from someone who began his career in a comedy troupe that became The State , MTV's short-lived 1990s cult sketch comedy series; hosted The Michael Showalter Showalter , a satirical talk show on CollegeHumor.com; and released a stand-up album called Sandwiches & Cats .

But for those who have followed Showalter's rather unusual path to becoming a Hollywood director, to see him now helming a major motion picture starring Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett is actually not too surprising.

For one thing, Showalter worked with Hathaway on The Idea of You , a 2024 romantic comedy-drama that he directed.

"She's a true artist; she gives 10,000 percent of herself to her work, and she's a wonderful human being," Showalter said of Hathaway in an interview with the Credits . "But I love working with her because of what she brings creatively. She has a million ideas, so much passion, and as a director, that's more than you could ever ask for. She is constantly trying to find ways to make her character more interesting and complicated; she's totally fearless and completely committed. Any opportunity I can get to work with her, I will always take."

But Showalter has worked with plenty of other A-listers too.

The Eyes of Tammy Faye : He directed Jessica Chastain and Andrew Garfield in this 2021 biographical drama that chronicles the rise and fall of televangelists Tammy Faye Bakker and Jim Bakker. Chastain won an Oscar for her portrayal of Tammy Faye.

The Dropout : He also directed the 2022 Hulu miniseries about the rise and fall of Elizabeth Holmes starring Amanda Seyfried, who won an Emmy Award for her portrayal of the disgraced Theranos founder. The show earned Showalter two Emmy nominations.

The Baxter : Showalter made his directorial debut in 2005 with this Brooklyn-set rom-com in which he starred alongside Elizabeth Banks, Michelle Williams and Justin Theroux, who plays his fiancée's old boyfriend who returns to her life just before their wedding.

Hello, My Name is Doris : In 2015, he directed Sally Field in a coming-of-age romantic comedy that drew critical praise, especially for Field. "She's funny, she's fragile, she's fierce, she's incedibly lovable," Showalter said of Field's performance . "And I think Sally encapsulates all of what we see in this character."

The Big Sick : In 2017, Showalter was again behind the camera for The Big Sick , another rom-com-dram, which earned an Oscar nomination for Best Screenplay for writers Kumail Nanjiani and Emily V. Gordon, and won the Critics Choice award for Best Comedy.

Wet Hot American Summer : Showalter's first brush with Hollywood success was with a 2001 ensemble comedy he cowrote and starred in alongside Paul Rudd, Amy Poehler, Bradley Cooper (in his big screen debut), Molly Shannon, Elizabeth Banks and other former members of The State .

For Verity , which was adapted from Colleen Hoover's bestselling novel of the same name , Showalter said he was inspired by old Alfred Hitchcock movies and '80s and '90s erotic thrillers, including Fatal Attraction , Basic Instinct , Body Double and Jagged Edge .

"Jagged Edge is one of the movies that inspired me," he told the Credits. "I don't think that's a movie a lot of people know now. One thing I love about Jagged Edge is how glamorous it is. The actors are so good-looking, the clothes are so nice, and the locations are so gorgeous. Hitchcock's Hollywood films in the 1950s also have a sense of glamour. They felt incredibly aspirational and escapist."

Showalter said he was also inspired by Hoover's book, which he described as "twisted, dirty, and a little kinky" — elements he wanted to bring back to the big screen.

"I think that, for whatever reason, that primal sexuality you saw in those movies where there's carnal attraction — that deep, primal thing that you see in an erotic thriller — for a time was at odds with some of the things going on culturally," Showalter told Variety . "And maybe, for whatever reason, people are open to it again in a way that they hadn't been for a while."

Verity will be released in theaters on Oct. 2.

articles.title: New movies to watch this weekend: See 'Verity' and 'Digger' in theaters, rent or buy 'Coyote vs. Acme,' stream 'Evil Dead Burn' on HBO Max
articles.summary: Colleen Hoover gets a star-studded new adaptation and Tom Cruise makes a big swing — but you might be better off renting a controversial Looney Tunes flick a...
articles.body:
Welcome to Trust Me, I Watch Everything , a weekly guide to notable new movies opening or becoming available each Friday.

This week's buzziest releases are Verity, the latest Colleen Hoover adaptation with the most A-list cast yet, and Digger, an obnoxious Tom Cruise Oscar play that's expected to bomb miserably .

If you'd rather stay home, you can rent or buy Coyote vs. Acme, which is newly available after its theatrical run. The movie that was once shelved for a tax write-off has officially grossed over $100 million globally. You can also check out The Uprising with Andrew Garfield.

Want to stick to a streaming service you're likely already paying for? Evil Dead Burn hits HBO Max , and Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma debuts on Mubi. 'Tis the season for horror, after all!

But the list truly goes on and on, so let's dive in!

My colleague Kelsey Weekman covered this one!

Why you should probably skip it: We can't talk about Verity the movie without first talking about Verity the book.

It's a novel by Colleen Hoover, the modern queen of WTF-romance who's also responsible for It Ends with Us. I really can't overstate her impact: She outsold the Bible in 2022 and built a pop-star-level fan army to become one of the few living authors considered a household name. Hoover's books, which are wildly popular on the bookish side of the internet, are soapy, emotional and — let's be honest — pretty bad. But that's what makes them delicious. And Verity is the most delicious of them all. It's a one-star book that offers a five-star reading experience.

In the film, Dakota Johnson plays a struggling novelist named Lowen who's hired to take over a popular series as ghostwriter after its original author, Verity (Anne Hathaway), is incapacitated. Lowen moves into Verity's home, becomes entangled with Verity's husband Jeremy (Josh Hartnett) and uncovers Verity's disturbing autobiographical writing that may be evidence of a crime.

I found myself begging the cinematic gods that the movie version of Verity would feel just as ridiculous as the book. It's an erotic thriller that's heavy on bonkers plot points. For instance, it opens with Lowen witnessing a car crash and getting blood spattered all over her clothes right before an important meeting. Later, she bites her headboard at the exact same place Verity once left bite marks. No spoilers, but Verity is portrayed as so ghoulishly cruel toward her children that she might as well be a cartoon witch.

The movie preserves many of the book's wilder happenings, but Hoover's quirkily absurd writing style is extracted from the screen, which sucks the campiness right out of it. It's not bad enough to be good in a fun way, but it's also not good enough to be authentically good. Hathaway, in her fifth movie of the year , seems to be having the most fun. And I appreciated that it's likely the first movie to feature a Hot Ones interview as a major plot point.

I once gleefully watched videos about the book titled " Verity by Colleen Hoover is an unhinged dumpster fire. And that's an understatement." and " Verity by Colleen Hoover is literally the WORST book ever written". But I could never summon that much emotion to talk about the movie, which is ultimately just fine.

What other critics are saying: The ones who like it find it fun and campy , but the ones who don't went hard. "A flat-footed dud, at once overwrought and underplotted, and barely propped up by A-list stars who look either embarrassed, confused or indifferent to be there," Variety's Guy Lodge writes . TheWrap's Amelia Emberwing says Verity has its issues, but it "feels like the perfect movie to put on with your girlfriends."

How to watch: Verity is now playing in theaters nationwide.

Why you should skip it: Tom Cruise steps outside of his death-defying blockbuster comfort zone and stars in an ambitious and expensive arthouse film directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu, a filmmaker beloved by The Academy and the man behind Oscar-winning films like The Revenant and Birdman. It's Cruise's first "big swing" in arguably 20 years or more.

Unfortunately for audiences, it's an excruciating, insufferable, direly unfunny and pretentious slog that's self-aware in a way that completely undercuts the entire premise of the movie, literally arguing against its own utility. It's so decidedly audience-unfriendly — the exact opposite of a crowd-pleaser — that I almost have to begrudgingly respect it for existing, especially at this size, scale and pedigree. Almost!

Cruise stars as Digger Rockwell, a billionaire oil man who is portrayed as the most powerful man in the world, way moreso than the U.S. president. He embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity's savior before the disaster he personally unleashed destroys everything.

It's an attempt at satire about a world that prizes corporate profits over everything, but it's never funny, nor is it saying anything new or interesting. The "jokes" that are there are so broad and obvious and eyeroll-inducing that you'll have a hard time believing that's what they went with. Imagine Dr. Strangelove if it sucked, or Don't Look Up if it were more obnoxious and less funny.

There's a major element of the movie that's been kept entirely out of the marketing, and I won't spoil it here, but it's insulting to the audience and completely deflating as a narrative device. Without getting into specifics, let's just say the movie becomes self-aware in a way that took me right out of it, and made me wonder why the hell I would want to spend any more time watching.

This reveal, in a cruel twist of fate, is the only funny moment in the entire movie, and it's one that's meant to be taken deadly seriously. To present something so objectively terrible that 40 minutes in, the filmmaker cuts in to say, "Don't worry, this is terrible for good reason" is frankly astonishing. The acting is so over-the-top that the movie has to pump the brakes and acknowledge it before moving on with the rest, which remains the same type of bad. It's stunning!

The movie's messaging is ultimately, "making art about the world's ills is futile, we're all doomed anyway, and you, the person watching this movie, are stupid for expecting to get anything meaningful out of this overly theatrical and didactic garbage."

Watching Digger is an experience akin to being scolded for something you had no part in. The movie aims to take billionaires and those in power down a peg, but the people watching the movie are not billionaires and are likely not in a power position in the government. What does Iñárritu expect me to do about any of this?

Cruise is an incredible actor in addition to being our Last Movie Star, but he's so bad here that he's more likely to earn a Razzie nomination than the Oscar nod so many pundits expect to happen. Digger Rockwell is more of a sketch-comedy caricature than a compelling character you'd want to spend two hours with; constantly bloviating and hamming it up with zero subtlety. You'd get sick of this guy in a six-minute SNL bit.

Digger is easily one of the worst movies of the year, rendered worse by its own messaging that movies such as this don't do anything to help the cause and are actually stupid. If you say so!

What other critics are saying: It's a swing and a miss, mostly. Time's Stephanie Zacharek writes, "Iñárritu and his star aren't telling us a story; they're selling us, relentlessly, on the genius of the movie they've made. This is reverse-engineered awards bait, a movie that insists it's digging for the truth, when all it's really doing is shoveling." Monica Castillo at AV Club writes, " Digger lacks emotional depth, being much more interested in the showmanship of tricks and razzle-dazzle than character development. While Cruise puts on a good show, he's walking around the loose threads of the script to get there."

How to watch: Digger is now playing in theaters nationwide .

Beware Boiúna: This "giant snake killing people in the Amazon" movie, sadly, does not feature enough of its titular giant snake killing people in the Amazon. It takes a full hour before we get any real snake action, and when we do, it's obfuscated by quick-cut editing and what surely has to be a low VFX budget. There's a misdirect that I appreciated in theory, but even that moment feels more anticlimactic rather than the "Oh, s***!" reaction they're clearly going for. Take a shot every time a character says something akin to, "She decides who lives and who dies" or "This is her domain." It's a disappointment from horror filmmaker Mike P. Nelson (the Wrong Turn and Silent Night, Deadly Night reboots), who just got the gig directing the next Saw movie. Let's hope that one delivers more than this. Get tickets .

Why you should see it: It's been three years since Warner Bros. decided that Coyote vs. Acme would be better for the company's bottom line if it were shelved indefinitely for a tax write-off rather than get a theatrical or even a streaming release.

Now, thanks to a smaller independent movie production company called Ketchup Entertainment — which also rescued another Looney Tunes movie that WB put on the chopping block, 2024's The Day the Earth Blew Up featuring Daffy Duck and Porky Pig — Coyote vs. Acme is triumphantly back from the dead.

The great irony of the entire ordeal, which led to tons of backlash for Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav and a groundswell of protests, online and in-person , demanding the movie be released, is that it's actually the best Looney Tunes movie ever made, by far.

The bar isn't exactly high; people my age likely have nostalgic affection for Space Jam, but it's not on the same level as Coyote vs. Acme, which feels more inspired by Who Framed Roger Rabbit? than other existing Looney Tunes hybrid live-action efforts.

After Acme products fail him one too many times in his dogged pursuit of the Roadrunner, Wile E. Coyote decides to hire a billboard lawyer (hilariously played by Saturday Night Live alum Will Forte) to sue the Acme Corporation, which is revealed to have nefarious motives for their faulty line of products. And perhaps Coyote has some secret motivations of his own for wanting to go to court.

The movie, already an underdog story, takes on a new resonance amid the drama surrounding its release. It opens with text that jokes, "based on a true story," which makes you wonder whether they added that after all the WB turmoil. As film critic Matt Singer puts it, "I will leave it to you, dear reader, to decide why a studio in the midst of a massive merger with another studio would choose not to release a highly entertaining legal thriller about a cartoonishly evil mega-corporation engaged in conspiracies to maintain monopolistic control over the economy through their shady connections with a willfully ineffectual government."

The movie's integration of the cartoons into live action is easily the best in its field since Roger Rabbit . The cartoon violence is there to make the kids laugh, as effective a strategy as it ever was, and the adults get legal courtroom-drama gags cleverly modeled after Looney Tunes-esque mayhem.

The script from unlikely scribe Samy Burch, writer of the very adult Todd Haynes film May December , engages with the characters in a way I didn't expect and even found a bit moving. Using the Wile E. Coyote and Road Runner cartoons to tell a story about dogged perseverance in the face of systemic oppressive forces conspiring against you sounds silly, and it absolutely is. The fact that it works so well onscreen is a testament to Burch's writing. And the entire debacle with its release strategy only makes its message that much more resonant.

Coyote vs. Acme is an unlikely and unexpected delight with a lot of heart, thankfully meeting the moment of its rallying cry against executive interference in art with its meta-commentary on corporate greed.

What other critics are saying: It's immediately beloved! Amy Nicholson of the Los Angeles Times writes , "Wile E. Coyote isn't asking for a handout. If anything, he's a true believer in the American Dream, willingly and literally breaking his back to put food on his table." Tim Robey at the Telegraph writes, "While the novelty factor wears off after a while, what Dave Green's film gets bang on is reconsidering the eternal enmity between Coyote and Road Runner as a form of love story — a game of endless pursuit, catch me if you can."

How to watch: Coyote vs. Acme is now available to rent or buy on Apple TV , Prime Video and other VOD platforms.

Why you should maybe watch it: This perfectly serviceable but rather dull historical action film is overtly political and doesn't have to tie itself in knots to make connections between the 1381 Peasants' Revolt in England and how wealth and power function today. It's not subtle about it; the rebelling commoners are at one point referred to as "deplorables."

Andrew Garfield plays the leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II, forming an army of the people to face the king's might in a fight for justice.

The most interesting thing about this movie is, unfortunately, extratextual, as the U.S. marketing pivoted late in the game to calling it The Uprising: The Rise of Robin Hood and stressing that the film was "set against the true events of the uprising that helped inspire the legend of Robin Hood," even as the non-U.S. marketing departments insisted that it was not, in fact, about Robin Hood.

I can confirm, dear reader, that the movie does, in fact, pivot to a stealth origin story for Robin Hood eventually, much like it unfolded in the press: at the absolute last minute! It's far more compelling as a movie about the Peasants' Revolt than as a Robin Hood picture, and that's without getting into the muddying of timelines for those who care about historical accuracy.

What other critics are saying: It's a mixed bag. AP's Mark Kennedy writes, "[Director Paul] Greengrass has quite simply robbed his own movie. We did not come for this." Frank Scheck at the Hollywood Reporte r was into it, writing, "There's no doubting the commitment of everyone involved, from the superb cast ... to the technical craftspeople who evoke medieval England with such vividness that you can practically smell the church incense."

How to watch: The Uprising is now available to rent or buy on Apple TV, Prime Video and other VOD platforms.

📺 Movies newly available on streaming services you may already have

Why you should skip it: There are two types of Evil Dead fans nowadays. The first are those who adore the original Sam Raimi trilogy and its comic underpinnings, and consider the 2013 remake and everything that followed edgelord garbage. At their core, no matter how scary and creepy and cruel they can get, Raimi's Evil Dead movies are fun.

The 2013 remake, Evil Dead Rise and now Evil Dead Burn are far from fun. It's as if the main operating principle since then has been "no fun at all," replacing anything resembling it with as much over-the-top, bloody brutality as possible, and tossing in a heavy-handed metaphor about some sort of trauma, whether it's addiction in the 2013 version or an abusive family unit in Burn.

And then there are those who likely grew up with the 2013 movie, so to them, the Evil Dead franchise is all about being the goriest, meanest and cruelest, with characters mutilating themselves and others in the most creative and unexpected ways imaginable. I expect these folks were happy with Evil Dead Rise and will remain impressed with Evil Dead Burn.

There are certainly people out there who enjoy both modes, but for the sake of argument, let's ignore them. I, unfortunately, haven't enjoyed an Evil Dead movie since Raimi last directed one: 1992's Army of Darkness. (I have to imagine he's still upset about having the absolutely perfect title, Medieval Dead, replaced.)

In theory, I love that this franchise has morphed into a major studio horror franchise proving ground for hungry young genre filmmakers. But in execution, I am reminded each time of the lightning-in-a-bottle, no-budget quality of Raimi's trilogy and how the modern approach just fundamentally doesn't work for me, especially when tied to a metaphor about family and trauma and toxic, abusive relationships and male inadequacy and rage, because that's where the genre is at now.

In Evil Dead Burn, a recently widowed woman seeks solace with her late husband's family. As they transform one by one into Deadites, she discovers that the vows she took in life survive even in death. Because what could be scarier than some time with your in-laws?!

A series formula has now been established: We're introduced to some folks who will soon be Deadites, as the camera lingers on various household items that will certainly be used to kill them in the near future. This is meant as an allusion to the Raimi films, with updated versions of Ash's iconic chainsaw and "boomstick," but it lacks the playfulness and manic energy of that character and those movies.

Burn has a New French Extremity feel to its violence, thanks to French filmmaker Sébastien Vaniček, whose terrific Infested, now streaming on Shudder, led Raimi to hire him. Vaniček has fun placing the camera in unlikely places and adding his own touch to some classic Raimi tricks, but the deadly serious subject matter here is a big miss, especially given how poorly written the characters are. As I mentioned earlier, Evil Dead movies are supposed to be fun and scary, and Burn opts for an upsetting and dour route instead with an allegory about domestic violence and inherited male rage.

Evil Dead is the last horror franchise I'd expect to fall victim to the "every horror movie is a treatise on grief or inherited trauma," but it's absolutely going for that here. That said, it's admirably mean-spirited, and Vaniček does a solid job of paying homage to Raimi while also making it his own. Ultimately, however, the film lacks the inventive comedic sensibilities that set Evil Dead apart from other iconic horror series. Fans who consider the 2013 film and its buckets of blood to be the model, though, will likely be more entertained.

What other critics are saying: It's getting far stronger reviews than mine. Owen Gleiberman at Variety dug it, writing, "The violence, while nonstop, remains aggressively 'thematic,' as the bottled-up family tensions and angers come out in the form of gnashing, bashing, gouging, severing, impaling, dismembering." Monica Castillo at AV Club agrees with me, though, writing, "It's a misfit standalone entry that has moments of humor and striking camera moves but ventures into too-serious territory in such a way that it loses the Evil Dead spirit of guilt-free chaos."

How to watch: Evil Dead Burn is now streaming on HBO Max .

Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma: Jane Schoenbrun's follow-up to the extremely personal I Saw the TV Glow is arguably even more personal, exploring an extremely specific feeling while saying so much about horror movies, sexuality, identity, shame and the intersection of all these things that it doesn't matter if you don't personally connect to every single element. Unlike its predecessor, which is deeply moving but also fairly humorless, Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma is laugh-out-loud funny and joyful. It couldn't be further in tone from TV Glow despite exploring similar ideas. It's fun ! Read my full review here . Now streaming on Mubi .

That's all for this week! We'll see you next Friday, when the big releases are The Social Reckoning, Animals and Other Mommy .

Looking for more recs? Find your next watch on the Yahoo 100 , our daily list of the most popular movies of the year.

articles.title: Big fan of Michael McDonald gets an even bigger surprise: he’s his son
articles.summary: Michael Goessling grew up a big fan of Michael McDonald and The Doobie Brothers only to discover the musician is his biological father.
articles.body:
Michael Goessling remembers being eight years old and grooving to The Doobie Brothers.

"I was a crazy Doobie Brothers fan and people remember me singing along to 'China Grove' and listening to their music like 'Black Water' back in the day," the now 59-year-old said in an interview. "I was always a bit of a music nut and it's starting to make sense nowadays."

That's because Goessling now knows that the group's legendary lead singer, Michael McDonald, is his biological father.

Goessling has had to pinch himself since learning a year ago that he is the product of a teen relationship between McDonald and a woman Goessling identified only as "Diane" — who were both 14 when they discovered they were expecting a baby.

"Initially they thought that maybe they would just go ahead and get married and figure it out and count on and rely on their family to support them," Goessling said. "But ultimately the parents had other ideas and it was determined collectively that I would be placed for adoption through Catholic Charities."

He was adopted by Paul and Kay Goessling and had an idyllic childhood in Missouri, well loved and raised with siblings.

Fast forward to about 15 years ago when Goessling, as an adopted child, registered with the genetic testing company 23andMe to try and determine if there were any medical issues he might have inherited from his biological parents as he was about to become a father himself.

All the tests came back normal and Goessling considered closing out his file with the company but said he had a "gut feeling" that he should leave it active.

Good thing too given that a year ago Michael McDonald's son Dylan, with his wife Amy Holland, used the site to track Goessling down, Goessling said.

Goessling said he learned that the younger McDonald and his sister Scarlett were aware that they had a half sibling somewhere and also knew that their father had never given up wanting to meet the son that had been given up for adoption.

"He found me instantly and got an email saying 'Michael Goessling, St. Louis, Missouri, half brother.'"

Goessling first connected with his birth mother, and then with McDonald, a five-time Grammy winner who, with The Doobie Brothers, was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2020.

Goessling has been a huge fan of McDonald as both a member of The Doobie Brothers and a solo artist and had even attended a few of his concerts over the years.

"I'm still trying to get my head around this whole thing," Goessling said. "I still wake up a year later and my first thought is I'm waking up from the craziest dream still, still to this day."

McDonald told CNN affiliate WSMV Channel 4 in Nashville, Tennessee, that he had carried guilt about the adoption for years, before finally connecting with Goessling in 2025.

"But just to know that he was ok and that he had a good life and I life certainly that I probably wouldn't have been able to afford him at that time in my life was…a great reward," McDonald told the station.

A request for additional comment has been sent to McDonald's representatives.

Now the pair are tickled that they share the same name despite the fact that Goessling was unnamed at the time of his closed adoption and his adopted parents had no idea the names of his biological parents.

They also share similar facial hair which heightens their resemblance. Goessling credits his wife Nicole for that as she encouraged him to grow his beard during the pandemic.

Goessling is glorying in now having a relationship with his birth parents whom he cannot praise enough for being wonderful people and wishes his dad, Paul, had lived long enough to see the big, beautiful blended family they have all become.

In addition to being talented, Goessling said he found McDonald funny, smart, kind and said he shares his passion for advocating for adoption which is part of the reason why they are happy to speak about it publicly now as they hope the spotlight on their story will shine a light on the issue.

The pair also share a love for music as Goessling plays a bit of guitar and also sings. As for how well he sings, he chuckled when he shared that in no way does he sound like McDonald.

"I did not inherit the voice," Goessling laughed. "God only made one of those."

articles.body:
A chuva que atinge Espírito Santo desde a madrugada deste sábado (3) provocou o cancelamento de oito voos, adiou o show de Marcelo Falcão e impediu a chegada de dois chefs a um festival gastronômico em Vitória . O mau tempo também levou à suspensão de missas no Convento da Penha e causou alagamentos em ruas de Vila Velha, na Grande Vitória.

Segundo o Instituto Capixaba de Pesquisa, Assistência Técnica e Extensão Rural (Incaper), a presença de umidade vinda do oceano favoreceu a formação de nuvens de chuva em grande parte do estado.

Para domingo (4), o Incaper prevê ventos de norte e nordeste e tempo predominantemente aberto no estado.

A previsão indica períodos de maior nebulosidade durante a madrugada e início da manhã, seguidos de abertura de sol e elevação das temperaturas à tarde.

Para este sábado, havia previsão de períodos de sol, mas também de chuva ocasional no Sul, na região Serrana e na Grande Vitória.

Saguão do aeroporto de Vitória outubro de 2026. Chuva no Espírito Santo cancela voos — Foto: Reprodução/TV Gazeta

No Aeroporto de Vitória, oito voos foram cancelados durante a manhã deste sábado por causa das condições meteorológicas, segundo a Zurich Airport Brasil.

Os voos tinham como origem ou destino os aeroportos de Guarulhos, Congonhas e Galeão. Os passageiros foram orientados a procurar as companhias aéreas para informações e remarcações.

Marcelo Falcão no Festival de Inverno Bahia (FIB) 2026 — Foto: Laecio Lacerda / Divulgação

Também por causa da chuva, o show de Marcelo Falcão, que seria realizado neste sábado em Vitória, foi adiado para 17 de outubro, às 16h.

O voo do cantor chegou a decolar, mas não conseguiu pousar na capital capixaba. A produção informou que tentou alternativas com a companhia aérea, mas não conseguiu viabilizar a apresentação.

Os ingressos já comprados continuam válidos para a nova data. Quem preferir o reembolso pode solicitar a devolução.

No Salt, Fire & Drive Festival, os chefs Henrique Fogaça e Léo Santos também não conseguiram chegar a Vitória.

Os voos retornaram aos aeroportos de origem depois que o aeroporto da capital foi temporariamente fechado por causa da chuva.

A organização tentou remarcar a participação dos chefs, mas não conseguiu devido à instabilidade do tempo e a outros compromissos.

O festival, no entanto, continua neste sábado, domingo (4) e domingo (5), no estacionamento externo coberto do Shopping Vitória. A aula-show do chef Fernando Kawasaki foi mantida.

Chuva no ES cancela voos e missas no Covento da Penha, adia show e provoca alagamentos; veja a previsão — Foto: Reprodução

Em Vila Velha, moradores registraram ruas alagadas em bairros como Itapuã, Cocal, Nova Itaparica, Novo México e na Avenida Leila Diniz, na região do Ibes.

As prefeituras de Vila Velha, Cariacica e Vitória informaram à TV Gazeta que, até o momento, não haviam recebido chamados da Defesa Civil relacionados à chuva.

As missas no Convento da Penha, em Vila Velha, também foram suspensas neste sábado por causa das condições climáticas.

Nas redes sociais, um anúncio comunicava que devido às fortes chuvas a Missa do Tríduo prevista para 15h30 estava cancelada.

Informou também que, a partir das 12h, a área visitável do Convento da Penha estaria temporariamente fechada assim como a Capela de São Francisco e a Lanchonete também, permanecendo o acesso permitido somente até a área do Campinho.

A Ladeira da Penitência também ficou fechada, como medida preventiva, considerando as condições climáticas e os riscos naturais decorrentes da chuva, especialmente relacionados ao piso, às pedras e à possibilidade de quedas.

O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) emitiu três alertas de chuva para o Espírito Santo, válidos até as 23h59 deste sábado.

Há avisos amarelo, laranja e vermelho, com previsão que varia de até 50 milímetros a mais de 100 milímetros de chuva em 24 horas, além de possibilidade de ventos fortes, granizo, alagamentos, transbordamento de rios e deslizamentos.

O alerta vermelho, de maior severidade, abrange parte da Grande Vitória, a região Serrana e todo o Sul do Espírito Santo.

articles.title: Box Office: ‘Digger’ Nosediving With $3.4 Million on Opening Day, ‘Verity’ Lands at No. 1 With $15.1 Million on Friday
articles.summary: Not even a Tom Cruise-filled, all-stops-pulled press tour — including a GQ cover, a “New Heights” podcast appearance and a “Risky Business”-inspired jaunt do...
articles.body:
Not even a Tom Cruise-filled, all-stops-pulled press tour — including a GQ cover , a "New Heights" podcast appearance and a "Risky Business"-inspired jaunt down the "Jennifer Hudson Show" spirit tunnel — could keep "Digger" from flatlining at the box office.

Warner Bros.' R-rated black comedy generated $3.4 million from 3,321 North American theaters on Friday following a slew of negative reviews and divided word of mouth. The film is shaping up to be one of the year's biggest flops, with estimates of just $7.5 million domestically in its opening weekend. The film was greenlit at $125 million but ended up ballooning to $160 and $180 million after production ran long , according to knowledgeable sources. That's a problem because the studio splits ticket sales with theater owners, meaning "Digger" is primed to lose many millions in its theatrical run.

Directed by Academy Award winner Alejandro González Iñárritu, "Digger" stars Cruise as a powerful oil tycoon whose company sparks an ecological calamity. Despite Cruise's enduring star power, having anchored recent blockbusters like the "Mission: Impossible" franchise and 2022's sensation "Top Gun: Maverick," "Digger" will wind up as the latest misfire for Warner Bros. This year, the studio has siphoned off a string of duds including Maggie Gyllenhaal's punk rock "The Bride!" and DC's comic book adaptation "Supergirl."

With general audiences rejecting "Digger," Amazon MGM's psycho-thriller "Verity" took the top spot on Friday with $15.1 million from 3,510 North American theaters. The movie is expected to make $33.6 million domestically through the weekend.

Adapted from Colleen Hoover's bestselling book of the same name, "Verity" centers around famed author Verity Crawford (Anne Hathaway), who gets badly injured in a car accident, leaving her husband (Josh Hartnett) to hire a struggling writer (Dakota Johnson) to finish the remaining books. Michael Showalter directed. It's Hoover's fourth novel to hit the big screen, following 2024's "It Ends With Us" (Sony), 2025's "Regretting You" (Paramount), and 2026's "Reminders of Him" (Universal).

Zach Cregger's zombie horror "Resident Evil" landed in second place on Friday, grossing $3.62 million. Starring Austin Abrams as a medical courier who must contend with a zombie outbreak while making a delivery to Raccoon City General Hospital, the Sony film looks to add $12 million by Sunday, bringing its domestic total to $124.395 million.

After "Digger's" third-place finish, Paramount Pictures' "The Heart of the Beast" followed with $3.15 million, bringing its cumulative gross to $38.39 million. The Brad Pitt-led adventure film was directed by David Ayer and stars the actor as a retired veteran who navigates a 58-mile trek to safety after he and his combat dog survive a plane crash in the Alaskan wilderness.

Finally, in fifth, was A24's "Primetime." The film grossed $2.49 million on Friday and should pull in another $7.5 million by Sunday. The film's opening weekend registered as the third-best for A24 behind "Backrooms" ($81.4 million) and "Civil War" ($25.5 million), and the Robert Pattinson-led drama has pulled in $28.58 million domestically thus far.

"Primetime" chronicles Chris Hansen's time as the host of Dateline NBC's "To Catch a Predator." While the film has received positive reviews and word of mouth since its debut at the Venice Film Festival earlier this month, the real-life Hansen has been less than complimentary ahead of the film's release; after seeing the film, Hansen called it "so bizarre and so in-and-out of reality," as well as "detached from reality."

articles.title: Cult-favorite movie's iconic Route 66 cafe faces uncertain future as highway turns 100
articles.summary: The Bagdad Cafe on historic Route 66 in California faces an uncertain future after its longtime owner's death as America's Mother Road turns 100.
articles.body: One of Route 66's best-known California landmarks is fighting to keep its doors open as America's "Mother Road" celebrates its 100th anniversary. The Bagdad Cafe in Newberry Springs has welcomed travelers from around the world for decades, but its future remains uncertain following the death of longtime owner Andrea Pruett in January and years of financial struggles that forced the closure of its kitchen. The quirky Mojave Desert spot, which is covered with dollar bills, flags, license plates and jerseys from around the world, became internationally famous after inspiring the 1987 German film "Bagdad Cafe." MAN REMORTGAGES HOME TO ENSURE BELOVED PUB REMAINS COMMUNITY CORNERSTONE Visitors can visit the cafe for photos and souvenirs, like T-shirts — which have become one of the its main sources of income — but it no longer serves food as the owners work to raise money and restore the kitchen and septic system. It also sells replica boomerangs designed by Alan Scott Craig, who appeared in the film, according to the cafe's website. TEXAS BBQ JOINT TAKES DRASTIC STEP AS SOARING BEEF PRICES DEVOUR RESTAURANT Many American visitors stop because of the highway's history, while European tourists, particularly from France, often make the trip because of the 1987 film, a worker told Fox News Digital. The cafe has accumulated about 40 guest books filled with messages from visitors over the decades, he said. Pruett owned the cafe for more than 30 years and became known for greeting travelers from around the globe. Those who worked alongside her welcoming visitors with a smile and sometimes climbing onto the counter to sing with French tourists visiting the cafe. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Before her death at age 85, she wrote in a GoFundMe post that international tourists and tour buses once accounted for roughly 80% of the business before the COVID-19 pandemic forced the cafe to shut its doors temporarily. When it reopened, it could only offer cold drinks instead of meals. But the pandemic hasn't been the cafe's only struggle. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Years of roof leaks left rainwater pouring into the 1950s-era building, threatening the memorabilia left behind by visitors over the decades, KTLA reported. In 2024, supporters raised enough money through a GoFundMe fundraiser to replace the roof and interior ceiling. A separate GoFundMe is now seeking donations to reopen the cafe's kitchen and upgrade its septic system. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES The next goal is reopening the kitchen before preserving the historic stop for future travelers, according to the cafe's website. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Pruett family has said it is still determining the landmark's long-term future, the Los Angeles Times reported, but the cafe remains open daily for visitors looking to experience the iconic stop along historic Route 66 upon its centennial year.

articles.title: El mensaje de agradecimiento de Paco González... en el que confiesa que iba a dejar la radio
articles.standfirst: Emotivas palabras del periodistas en la Cope
articles.summary: Emotivas palabras del periodistas en la Cope
articles.body: Paco González, director de 'Tiempo de Juego' de la Cadena Cope, sorprendió este sábado con un emotivo mensaje de agradecimiento... en el que desveló que tenía la intención de dejar la radio para dar más tiempo a su familia. El periodista madrileño, que cumple 60 años el próximo martes después de 40 en la radio, comenzó su intervención en el programa con un inesperado discurso. Confesó que tenía pensado dejarlo ya, pero, dice, va a hacerlo de otra forma... siguiendo al frente. Paco dijo que no era una carta, pero que si lo fuera, era de agradecimiento y así desveló su intención de 'colgar' el micrófono que, de momento, queda para más adelante. "Si esto fuera una carta, sería una carta de agradecimiento, no de despedida. Uno se va haciendo viejo y casco 60 el próximo martes. Esta sería mi temporada 40 en la radio... Total, que como con la edad uno se vuelve más emotivo, al menos yo, y le apetece más el pueblo que la ciudad y la tranquilidad que el ruido y no sé qué... Pues, digo, voy a soltar esta chapita hoy para quedarme a gusto. Entonces, si les digo la verdad, yo tenía una sana intención que era... dejarlo". "Le tengo que dar gracias a Dios por la carrera impresionante que me ha dado, darle gracias a Dios por la radio, pero le tengo que dar más gracias por otro tesoro mayor, que es mi familia... y mi sana intención era quitarle tiempo a la radio para dárselo a mi familia. Quitarle todo el tiempo a la radio para dárselo a mi familia. Javier Visiers, que es nuestro jefe y es una persona en la que tengo una confianza absoluta y le quiero un montón, pensaba que era mejor hacerlo de otra forma. Entonces, lo vamos a hacer de otra forma, pero eso no me quita las ganas el seguir. Sigo en Cope, sigo en 'Tiempo de Juego', sigo en 'El Partidazo', no me quita las ganas de ser agradecido con los casi 40 años de carrera". "Agradecido, en primer lugar a los oyentes, también a los anunciantes, que son de lo que vivimos... Pero, en primer lugar por encima de todo, a los oyentes porque si esta historia de una carrera tan longeva ha tenido sentido ha sido gracias a ustedes. Muy pocos oyentes pueden presumir de hacer a un programa líderes en dos cadenas distintas. En la historia de la radio no sé cuántos programas han sido líderes en dos cadenas distintas. Pues ustedes, sí, lo hicieron una vez y lo han vuelto a hacer". "También quiero dar las gracias a las emisoras en las que he estado. A la Cadena Ser, que me dio una formación, me dio todas las oportunidades... y a la Cadena Cope, que me ha dado todas las oportunidades, todos los medios y, además, todo el afecto, que, como ya les he dicho, uno que está sensible, lo agradece más que nada". "Por supuesto, quiero dar las gracias a todos los compañeros, a los de la redacción de deportes que tenemos ahora que, por cierto, es la mejor redacción que yo he conocido en ninguna emisora de radio años luz. Habrán visto que no he querido decir nombres en el asunto de compañeros porque es que estaría hasta pasado mañana y no contaríamos el partido de España-Chequia, pero en realidad tendría que haber dicho por lo menos uno encarnando a todos los demás, que es Jorge Hevia, que es el alma del programa, el padre y la madre de Tiempo de Juego. Y ya está..." "Esta, repito, no es una carta, pero si lo fuera sería de agradecimiento y de gratitud por tantos años al filo de cumplir los 60. Decía Anthony Hopkins en 'Conoces a Joe Black' que 60 años, un suspiro... Bueno, no ha sido un suspiro, pero la verdad es que las cosas se pasan rápido... y tan feliz. Tengo el mejor trabajo del mundo. Vuelvo a darle gracias a Dios y tengo la mejor familia del mundo y estoy deseando estar con mi mujer, mis hijos, mis hermanos, todos juntos".

articles.title: 'Caddyshack' star Michael O'Keefe claims cocaine was budgeted on set, admits filming scenes high
articles.summary: Michael O'Keefe opens up about rampant cocaine use on the "Caddyshack" set, saying people treated the drug "like it was toothpaste" in the '70s.
articles.body: Michael O'Keefe is getting candid about what it was like on the set of the hit 1980 movie "Caddyshack." During a recent interview with Page Six, the 71-year-old actor shared that there was a lot of cocaine on the set of the classic comedy and claimed the drug was even accounted for in the movie's budget, with the actor noting, "there was some miscellaneous item." "It was the 70s," he said. "That’s what was happening back then. People were just treating it like it was toothpaste, and you had to do it twice a day to stay healthy." The movie was filmed in 1979 and released in 1980, and also starred Ted Knight, Chevy Chase, Bill Murray and Rodney Dangerfield and was set at the fictional Bushwood Country Club. TOM HARDY'S 'MOBLAND' DRAMA TOPS HOLLYWOOD'S MOST NOTORIOUS ON-SET MELTDOWNS AND FEUDS When reflecting on the drug use on set, O'Keefe recalled doing cocaine before filming certain scenes, telling Page Six that when he watches those scenes now, "it was not my favorite memory," and that he is "not too happy about them." "But I can report to you that right after that movie, during that movie, was the last time I ever did anything like cocaine," he said. "I realized that it was a terrible thing to get involved [with], and like so many things in the drug world, it looked like fun, but in reality, it wasn’t." Part of the reason he decided to take a step back from drugs was the death of Doug Kenney, who co-wrote and produced "Caddyshack." He called Kenney's death "a huge wake-up call." articles.title: Legendary filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao passes away at 94; ‘Aditya 369’ director mourned by celebrities, fans
articles.summary: Veteran filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao passed away at a private hospital in Chennai on Saturday, October 3, at the age of 94.
articles.body: Veteran filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao passed away at a private hospital in Chennai on Saturday, October 3, at the age of 94. The celebrated director had been undergoing treatment for age-related ailments, as reported by Telangana Today.Actor Vishnu Manchu was among those who expressed grief over the filmmaker's demise. Remembering the influence of Singeetham Srinivasa Rao's work on his own love for cinema, Vishnu described the director as a creative force who never restricted himself to established filmmaking conventions.Vishnu Manchu remembers Singeetham Srinivasa RaoVishnu Manchu shared an emotional tribute on social media. He recalled watching his films before understanding the technical aspects of filmmaking and said his respect for the veteran only increased as he entered the industry.“This loss feels deeply personal. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao garu was one of my favourite directors growing up. I watched his films with wonder, long before I fully understood the craft behind them.As I grew older and became a part of cinema myself, my admiration for him only grew stronger. He was a true lover of cinema. Fearless in his imagination, constantly experimenting, never allowing himself to be confined by a genre or a formula.Every film he made has something to teach us. Every film is a textbook. For me, he will always remain one of those filmmakers who made me fall in love with the magic of movies. We have lost a true legend, but his cinema will live on and continue to inspire generations. My heartfelt condolences to his family and loved ones. Rest in peace, Singeetham garu. Thank you for the cinema..”Fans pay tribute to the veteran directorNews of the filmmaker's death also drew emotional reactions from cinema enthusiasts on X.One fan wrote, “A Legend Leaves Us Singeetham Srinivasa Rao Garu, One of Indian cinema's most inventive filmmakers is no more. His cinema will remain immortal.” Another user posted, “Rest In Peace Legend You will forever live on in our memories. #SingeethamSrinivasaRao.”‘Aditya 369’ and other films that defined his careerBorn on September 21, 1931, Singeetham Srinivasa Rao worked as a director, screenwriter, producer, composer and actor. His career spanned Telugu, Kannada, Tamil, Hindi and English cinema. He directed approximately 60 films and earned a reputation for exploring unconventional ideas across different genres.His best-known works include ‘Aditya 369’, a science-fiction comedy that brought time-travel storytelling to Telugu cinema, and ‘Bhairava Dweepam’, a fantasy film rooted in folklore. Another notable work, ‘Pushpaka Vimana’, distinguished itself through its dialogue-free narrative. The movie had Kamal Haasan in the lead.From assistant director to award-winning filmmakerSingeetham Srinivasa Rao began his career as an assistant to acclaimed director K. V. Reddy. During this period, he worked on films such as ‘Mayabazar’ (1957) and ‘Jagadeka Veeruni Katha’ (1961). He made his directorial debut with the Telugu film ‘Neethi Nijayithi’ in 1972.His filmography also included socially relevant stories. ‘Dikkatra Parvathi’ (1974) won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Tamil, while ‘Tharam Marindi’ (1977) received the Nandi Award for Best Feature Film.A filmmaker who continued working into his ninetiesHis achievements included two National Film Awards, five Nandi Awards and three Karnataka State Film Awards. In 2011, the Film Federation of India honoured him with a Life Achievement Award.Singeetham Srinivasa Rao remained involved in filmmaking well into his nineties. articles.title: Ney Matogrosso tira as máscaras e as fantasias, mas não a trava emocional, em filme sobre os bastidores do artista | G1
articles.body:
Ney Matogrosso em imagem do documentário 'Ney por trás das máscaras', atração da mostra 'Premiére Brasil' do Festival do Rio 2026 — Foto: Divulgação

Direção: Esmir Filho com codireção de Thais Guisasola

Roteiro: Esmir Filho , João Maia e Thais Guisasola

♬ “Eu sou travado nessa questão emocional. Eu me seguro firme...”, admite Ney Matogrosso quase no fim do documentário “Ney por trás das máscaras”, filme exibido pela primeira vez na noite de ontem, sábado, 3 de outubro, como hors concours da mostra Première Brasil do Festival do Rio 2026.

A fala do artista dá o tom do filme em que o cineasta Esmir Filho – diretor do blockbuster “Homem com H” (2025), cinebiografia ficcional sobre a vida de Ney Matogrosso – desvenda os bastidores do cantor durante os preparativos da escola de samba Imperatriz Leopoldinense para o desfile em homenagem a Ney, apresentado pela agremiação no Carnaval de 2026 com o enredo “Camaleônico”.

Ney tira as máscaras, as fantasias e fica até nu diante das lentes de Esmir e da codiretora Thais Guisalosa – um desinibido nu frontal enquanto se seca após o banho – mas a trava emocional continua lá. Ney Matogrosso desnuda o corpo, mas não a alma.

Vê-se Ney em casa tomando café da manhã, interagindo no barracão da Imperatriz e na quadra da agremiação – e também obviamente no desfile propriamente dito – e ainda em camarins. Ouve-se nesses cenários o habitual discurso libertário de um artista que sempre se pautou pela ousadia.

Se o filme acompanhasse Ney somente nos bastidores do processo de criação do desfile da Imperatriz Leopoldinente, o foco de “Ney por trás das máscaras” teria ficado mais bem definido e original. Contudo, Esmir Filho abriu demais o foco.

Ney Matogrosso na Praça da Apoteose, cartão-postal do Carnaval carioca, no take inicial do filme 'Ney por trás das máscaras', de Esmir Filho — Foto: Divulgação

Há muitas cenas de Ney no habitat natural do artista, uma fazenda de 140 hectares, localizada em meio à Mata Atlântica, precisamente em Sampaio Correia, distrito de Saquarema (RJ), na Região dos Lagos do Rio de Janeiro. Lá, com a devida autorização do Ibama, Ney costuma soltar animais silvestres na mata. Vê-se no filme a soltura de uma jiboia.

“Ney por trás das máscaras” também mostra o cantor no camarim do estádio paulistano Nubank Parque durante os momentos que precederam a entrada em cena do artista em apresentação grandiosa do show da turnê “Bloco na rua”. A questão é que, nesse quesito, o filme de Esmir perde pontos, pois, em outro documentário, “Olho nu” (2014), lançado há 12 anos, o cineasta Joel Pizzini já fez o espectador enxergar Ney Matogrosso pelas frestas de palcos e matas no limite da liberdade consentida pelo artista.

Além de descortinar os bastidores do Carnaval, mostrando o cantor em contato com costureiras das fantasias da Imperatriz Leopoldinense e com demais trabalhadores da escola, agindo sem qualquer traço de afetação ou estrelismo, o documentário “Ney por trás das máscaras” se diferencia por desvendar um pouco a relação do artista com a mãe, Beita de Souza Pereira (1922 – 2026), falecida aos 103 anos, em março deste ano.

Tudo pode soar interessante para quem é fã do cantor. Mas, se Ney solta a jiboia, ele mesmo nunca se solta realmente diante das câmeras e, com isso, o documentário é que fica travado , sem nunca chegar efetivamente à apoteose .

Whoever is responsible for this should not be spared. They must face the harshest possible legal consequences and be made an example of. We must not let this go. When did we become so insensitive to each other? What kind of parenting is going on? What kind of society are we living in? Where do we find joy in degrading each other?. At a time when the world is debating and fearing how AI disrupts livelihoods and takes away jobs, these idiots are using that very technology to do utter nonsense. This is the digital equivalent of s*xual assault. The law must treat such acts with utmost seriousness. And to the team standing up against this, you have my full support".Jr NTR vows legal action against morphed ‘Chuttamalle’ videoJr NTR strongly condemned the creation of such distasteful videos and made it clear that legal action would follow. In his post, he wrote, "Disgusting, sick and shameless. In a land that worships women as mothers and goddesses, where 'Matrudevo Bhava' is not just a phrase but a part of our culture, some people have fallen so low that they are using AI to disrespect a woman in the most degrading way possible. Using AI to create something this vile is shameful beyond words."The actor continued, "To the scumbags behind this morphed Chuttamalle video, I will not spare any of you. I will take every possible legal action against those who created it and those who are spreading it. Please do not watch, share or engage with such content. Today it is someone else. Tomorrow, it could be your mother, sister, wife or daughter. This is a serious issue, and I urge all the state governments and the Government of India to act strongly and bring in strict regulations against the misuse of AI".About the original ‘Chuttamalle’ song‘Chuttamalle’ is a love song about the bond between the two main characters. The song is told from the heroine's side, played by Janhvi Kapoor, and shows how she feels when she is with her love, played by Jr NTR. The music is by Anirudh Ravichander, the lyrics are by Ramajogayya Sastry, the singer is Shilpa Rao, and the dance steps are by Bosco Martis. The song was also made in Tamil, Hindi, Kannada and Malayalam. The film, ‘Devara: Part 1’, stars Jr NTR, Janhvi Kapoor, Saif Ali Khan, Prakash Raj, Srikanth Meka, Tom Shine Chacko and Narain. It came out in theatres on September 27, 2024.Jr NTR plays two characters in the film, Devara and Varadha, and his role sits at the heart of the story. Kosaraju Hari Krishna and Sudhakar Mikkilineni produced it under the NTR Arts and Yuvasudha Arts banners, while Nandamuri Kalyan Ram presented it. articles.title: Phil Collins gets frank on marriage failures and life regrets: 'I regret my marriages falling apart'
articles.summary: Phil Collins told Piers Morgan his Genesis touring schedule destroyed his first marriage and revealed deep regrets about all three marriages falling apart.
articles.body: Phil Collins is opening up about his biggest regret throughout the course of his career. During a recent interview on "Piers Morgan Uncensored," the 75-year-old musician reflected on the toll his career took on his relationships with his children and how it affected his three marriages. "To some extent, I have to say I regret my marriages falling apart," he explained. "Sometimes I jumped. Well, one time I jumped, two times I was pushed. But I wouldn't have written it like that. But on the other hand, I've got five fantastic kids that I wouldn't have if that hadn't happened. So I have to balance it." The famous drummer was married to his first wife, Andrea Bertorelli, from 1975 to 1980. Collins adopted Bertorelli's daughter, Joely, and the couple welcomed son Simon. PHIL COLLINS' BRUSH WITH DEATH LEFT HIS CHILDREN PREPARING FOR THE UNTHINKABLE He also shares daughter Lily with his second wife, Jill Tavelman, whom he was married to from 1984 to 1996, and sons Nicholas and Mathew with his third wife, Orianne Cevey, whom he was married to from 1999 to 2006. When looking back on his first marriage, Collins admitted it broke down because he wasn't around, as he was touring with his band, Genesis, and couldn't be home. "Genesis did, in one year, I think, three American tours, two European tours, and a tour of Japan. And when I ended up getting separated from my first wife, the guys in the band said, ‘Well, why didn’t you tell us? We’d have stopped it.’ But that’s easy to say in retrospect," he said. "I was gone, and we grew apart." Despite his failure to make his relationships with his wives work, Collins said he "always tried to be there for the kids," and that he never planned on getting married three times, noting, "You don't go into life thinking that." articles.title: Pedro Pascal calls learning cello for ‘Behemoth!’ ‘hell and heaven’: ‘I took it everywhere’
articles.summary: Pedro Pascal takes on the challenge of learning the cello in just a week for his role in ‘Behemoth!’. Discover the struggles and triumphs he faced and how the music intertwined with his character's story.
articles.body: Pedro Pascal has learned plenty for his movie roles, but apparently nothing quite prepared him for the cello. For ‘Behemoth!’, Pascal plays Alex Serian, a gifted cellist whose life begins to unravel after he returns to Los Angeles. While the character may have spent years mastering the instrument, Pascal had only a fraction of that time to make it look convincing on screen.The actor opened up about the unusual preparation during the film’s New York Film Festival press conference on October 2, 2026. “The cello was the main character of my life for several weeks leading up to shooting. I took it with me everywhere I went,” Pascal said.That probably sounds slightly dramatic until he explained what learning the instrument actually involved. “Everything surprised me; it was hell ... and heaven,” he said, adding that he enjoyed being “in lessons again with another artist” and dealing with the “physical challenge” and “meticulousness” of playing the cello.Pedro Pascal had just a week to learn the celloPedro Pascal did not have the luxury of spending years becoming a convincing cellist. He explained that it can normally take as long as a year just to learn how to properly hold a cello bow. For ‘Behemoth!’, the process had to be “fast-tracked”, and Pascal had about a week.“I never caught up to it,” he admitted. Oddly enough, that became part of what he enjoyed about the experience.“I never caught up to it, which was kind of the ecstasy of it, I suppose,” Pascal said. “It was a joy, but it was the hardest thing that I’ve ever done creatively for a part.” His preparation even followed him to Vienna, where he had to cram in Mozart.The actor also remembered his first conversation with Tony Gilroy about whether he could actually pull the role off. Pascal was nervous and did not pretend he had all the answers. “I’m like, ‘I don’t know,’” he recalled.Why Pedro Pascal took the riskThe cello was not the only thing that made Pedro Pascal hesitate. He said the nonlinear story initially felt like a “challenge in a good way”. But there was something about the script that kept pulling him back.“I was so taken by what the story was and the kind of intimacy of all of it,” Pascal said, particularly the way it can feel intimate “to listen to music and to be guided by music.” That connection seems to have been enough to make him jump in, even without knowing whether he could master the instrument.‘Behemoth!’ premiered at the New York Film Festival on October 2, 2026, and is scheduled to open in US theatres on December 4, 2026. Film at Lincoln Center describes the film as a story about a cellist trying to pick up the pieces of a fractured life.CentreFor Pedro Pascal, though, the story started with a much more basic question: could he actually play the cello? His answer at the time was, essentially, “I don’t know.” He just decided to take the instrument everywhere and find out.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Taylor Swift pops into ‘SNL’ to joke around with host Dakota Johnson
articles.summary: Pop music icon Taylor Swift made a surprise appearance on “Saturday Night Live,” joining her friend and the episode’s host, Dakota Johnson, for some laughs.
articles.body: Pop music icon Taylor Swift made a surprise appearance on “Saturday Night Live,” joining her friend and the episode’s host, Dakota Johnson, for some laughs. Swift appeared on stage during Johnson’s opening monologue to address her role the movie star’s “literal therapist,” in Johnson’s words. “I’m not your therapist actually,” Swift said. “You just show up once a week at my house with an empty bottle of wine and ask if I want some.” Johnson agreed: “Yeah, well, I have manners.” Swift continued to describe a typical evening for the two. “You flop on my couch and overshare, and every so often I just say, ‘Damn that’s crazy,’” Swift said. Johnson, who has been a marquee presence in the “Fifty Shades” movie franchise, stars in the new movie “Verity” and appears in the new music video for Swift’s “Patient Zero.” She said Swift’s characterization of her role hosting the actor at home seems to describe “therapist.” But Swift had more to say about their nights. “And then I go, ‘Oh it’s getting late, I should probably go to bed,’ and then you say ... ” Johnson chimed in: “Sleepover — yay!” Their wine sessions end, Swift said, not with a sleepover, but with Pedialyte and a ride home via Swift’s security detail. Swift made another appearance during the curtain call, bringing out a blue and white cake for Johnson, who turned 37 on Sunday. “SNL” airs on NBC, a division of NBCUniversal, which is also the parent company of NBC News. articles.title: Michael J. Fox receives Canada’s highest honour for Parkinson’s advocacy
articles.summary: On October 2, 2026, Michael J. Fox received the prestigious Companion of the Order of Canada for his remarkable advocacy in Parkinson's research through the Michael J. Fox Foundation. Discover the significance of this honour and Fox's journey from actor to global advocate.
articles.body: Michael J. Fox has spent decades being recognised for the characters he played. On October 2, 2026, he received one of Canada’s biggest honours for something much more personal. The ‘Back to the Future’ star was promoted to Companion of the Order of Canada, the highest level of the country’s national honours system, during a ceremony at Rideau Hall in Ottawa.Fox was among 51 people inducted into or promoted within the Order of Canada that day. The Governor General’s Office recognised him for his global Parkinson’s advocacy, his openness about living with the disease and the work he has done through the Michael J. Fox Foundation. Governor General Louise Arbour also had a little fun with Fox’s most famous role during the ceremony.“After all, ‘Back to the Future’ has always been a much better idea than ‘Forward to the Past,’” she said, while praising Fox for choosing to use his public platform to support Parkinson’s research.Michael J. Fox turned his diagnosis into a bigger fightMichael J. Fox was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease in 1991, when he was 29. He kept the diagnosis private for several years before going public in 1998. In 2000, he founded the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson’s Research. What started with his own diagnosis has since grown into one of the biggest Parkinson’s research efforts in the world.The foundation says it has now funded $3 billion in global Parkinson’s research since it was established. And Fox is still pushing forward. On September 17, 2026, the foundation announced its $2.5 billion ‘All Grit. No Quit.’ campaign, aimed at speeding up research into new treatments and a cure.It is a striking number, but the reason behind the work is much simpler. Fox knows what it means to live with Parkinson’s, and he has spent years trying to make sure the people who come after him have better options.Michael J. Fox on why Canada still feels like homeMichael J. Fox, who was born in Edmonton, also spoke about what the honour meant to him personally. “It’s so many things,” he said after the ceremony, reflecting on growing up in Canada. He spoke about loving the country, its culture and the way it has “progressed and corrected course when it needed to, and stayed the course when it needed to.”That connection has stayed with him even after decades of living and working in the United States. At 65, Fox has a career that includes ‘Back to the Future’, ‘Family Ties’ and ‘Spin City’. But his legacy has grown beyond acting.The Order of Canada honour recognises that second chapter — the one that began with a diagnosis Fox once kept to himself and eventually became a global fight for Parkinson’s research. For Michael J. Fox, the road from actor to advocate was never something he planned. articles.body: Megastar Chiranjeevi has condemned the alleged misuse of artificial intelligence to create and circulate a digitally manipulated video involving Jr NTR and Janhvi Kapoor from their song ‘Chuttamalle’ in ‘Devara: Part 1’. He also said he plans to take up the matter with the Telugu Film Chamber, the Producers’ Council and other affiliated industry bodies.“I will take this matter up with the Telugu Film Chamber, the Producers’ Council and our affiliated industry bodies, and recommend the formation of a dedicated committee and support cell.”According to Chiranjeevi, such a mechanism should coordinate with Cyber Crime authorities to assist victims, facilitate the removal of manipulated content and pursue legal action against those responsible.The actor also urged the Central and State Governments to take stronger measures against the misuse of AI. Several celebrities have mourned his death, with Vijay Deverakonda remembering the filmmaker and his final directorial venture, 'Sing Geetham', in which the actor made a special cameo.Vijay Deverakonda remembers Singeetham Srinivasa RaoIn a tribute shared on X (previously Twitter), Vijay Deverakonda recalled his association with the veteran filmmaker and remembered the affection Singeetham had shown him over the years.“Singeetham sir. Your beliefs, your thoughts and your stories will live on with us forever. For everytime you called me since Pellichoopulu to shower love and effection, i hope it made you happy and brought a smile seeing me in one of your films - Sing Geetham. I feel happy to have been a part of one of your vision. My forever respect.”Singeetham's final directorial venture was 'Sing Geetham', described as an experimental musical comedy. He directed the film at the age of 94, with the project backed by 'Kalki 2898 AD' director Nag Ashwin. Ayaan Khan, Ahilya Bamroo and Shalini Kondepudi featured in the lead roles, while Vijay made a special appearance. The filmmaker's career spanned Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam and Hindi cinema, with his work often marked by experimentation and an unconventional approach to storytelling.Chiranjeevi mourns the filmmaker’s demiseChiranjeevi also paid tribute to Singeetham Srinivasa Rao, remembering him as a visionary filmmaker whose willingness to explore unfamiliar ideas left a lasting impression on Indian cinema.“Deeply saddened by the passing of the legendary filmmaker ‘Singeetam Srinivasa Rao’ garu. A true visionary, his imagination and courage to explore new ideas gave Indian cinema some of its most unforgettable films. His contribution to cinema will always be remembered with immense respect and affection.”Chiranjeevi also highlighted the filmmaker's enduring passion for cinema, pointing to Sing Geetham as an example of his continued creative spirit.“His recent film ‘Sing Geetham’ was a beautiful testament to his undying passion for storytelling. At heart, he remained forever young, curious and eager to create. My heartfelt condolences to his family and loved ones. We will miss you, Singeetam garu. Your films will continue to speak to generations. Om Shanti.”Singeetham Srinivasa Rao’s legacy in Indian cinemaSingeetham Srinivasa Rao built a diverse filmography across languages and genres during his decades-long career. Among his best-known works are the silent black comedy 'Pushpaka Vimana' (1987), the time-travel adventure 'Aditya 369' (1991) and the dance drama 'Mayuri' (1985). He also had a notable creative partnership with Kamal Haasan, collaborating with the actor on films including 'Apoorva Sagodharargal' (1989) and 'Michael Madana Kama Rajan' (1990). His work was distinguished by an openness to unusual concepts, experimental narratives and different cinematic forms.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ NEW POSTER has fans spotting Scarlet Witch clues as Anthony Mackie teases ‘a lot of doom’ in Robert Downey Jr. starrer
articles.summary: A new poster for ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ has sent Marvel fans into theory mode, with three mysterious figures appearing behind Doctor Doom in the latest
articles.body: A new poster for ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ has sent Marvel fans into theory mode, with three mysterious figures appearing behind Doctor Doom in the latest promotional artwork. The poster was unveiled during San Diego Comic-Con Málaga 2026 in Spain on October 3, prompting speculation that familiar Marvel Cinematic Universe characters could return. Meanwhile, Anthony Mackie has offered another tease about the upcoming film, promising audiences “a lot of doom”.‘Avengers: Doomsday’ poster sparks Wanda, Sylvie and Agatha theoriesAccording to the promotional material presented at San Diego Comic-Con Málaga 2026, Doctor Doom occupies the centre of the new ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ artwork, while three figures in coloured robes stand behind him. Their identities have not been revealed, but the mysterious silhouettes have already triggered speculation among Marvel fans.The red-robed figure has been linked by some fans to Wanda Maximoff, aka Scarlet Witch, played by Elizabeth Olsen. The character in green has similarly prompted theories about Sylvie, played by Sophia Di Martino in ‘Loki’. Meanwhile, the purple-robed figure has led to suggestions that it could be Agatha Harkness, played by Kathryn Hahn, or Clea, portrayed by Charlize Theron in ‘Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness’.These remain fan theories and have not been confirmed by Marvel Studios. The figures could also represent characters connected to Doctor Doom rather than established MCU heroes or villains.Marvel fans dissect mysterious figures in new posterThe speculation gained further momentum because similarly coloured figures were spotted during Marvel’s presentation at San Diego Comic-Con in California in July. Fans have since been attempting to connect the imagery with characters from across the MCU.One fan speculated that the purple figure could be Agatha Harkness, while another pointed to the colour of Wanda’s magic as a possible clue to her appearance in the film. However, none of these interpretations has been officially endorsed by Marvel Studios.With the identities of the three figures being deliberately kept under wraps, the poster appears to be giving fans plenty to decode ahead of the film’s release.Anthony Mackie teases ‘a lot of doom’ in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’Anthony Mackie, who attended the Málaga event alongside David Harbour and Winston Duke, also teased the scale of the threat in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’. The actor spoke about reuniting with Chris Evans and Sebastian Stan, joking about the trio wondering which of them might die in the upcoming film.“Whenever Chris Evans and Sebastian Stan and I get together, it’s like a powwow, like, we’re boys in the corner hanging out, laughing, joking and talking about what’s happening. Then we stop, Sebastian looks at both of us and goes, ‘So, which one of us is gonna die?’” Mackie said.He then offered a more direct hint about Doctor Doom’s presence in the story, saying, “I think the big thing is the amount of doom you’re going to see. It’s like every corner we turn, every time somebody speaks, it’s like, ‘Yo, there’s a lot of doom outside.’”Russo Brothers promise character moments in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’The Russo Brothers, who are directing ‘Avengers: Doomsday’, also sent a recorded message to attendees at the Málaga event. Mackie discussed the filmmakers’ ability to balance a huge ensemble while ensuring individual characters receive meaningful moments.“The Russo Brothers were great at giving every character and every person their moment. Every time I went to watch Endgame, every single character was given that moment for the audience to connect with them and breathe. And I think it’s the same with this movie,” Mackie said.Directed by Anthony and Joe Russo and written by Stephen McFeely, ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ features Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Chris Hemsworth, Channing Tatum, Simu Liu, Ian McKellen, Pedro Pascal, Paul Rudd, Anthony Mackie, Florence Pugh, Winston Duke, Alan Cumming and Wesley Holloway, among others.‘Avengers: Endgame Encore’ earns Rs 34.41 crore in IndiaMeanwhile, the 2026 re-release of ‘Avengers: Endgame’, titled ‘Avengers: Endgame Encore’, has reportedly collected Rs 34.41 crore in India net over nine days. Its India gross stands at Rs 40.88 crore, while the reported worldwide gross is also Rs 40.88 crore.According to Sacnilk, the English version accounts for Rs 24.09 crore of the India net total. It opened with Rs 5.25 crore on September 25, followed by Rs 5.60 crore on September 26 and Rs 5.20 crore on September 27. The collection dropped to Rs 1.50 crore on September 28 and remained at that level on September 29, before recording Rs 1.25 crore on each of the following two days. It then earned Rs 1.32 crore on October 2 and Rs 1.22 crore on October 3.The Hindi version has contributed Rs 6.52 crore, while the Telugu and Tamil versions have reportedly earned Rs 1.96 crore and Rs 1.84 crore, respectively, in India net.‘Avengers: Doomsday’ hype builds ahead of releaseWith Doctor Doom at the centre of the story and a sprawling ensemble bringing together several generations of MCU characters, ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ is already generating significant anticipation. The latest poster has added another layer of mystery, particularly with the identities of the three robed figures still unknown.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Taylor Swift surprises Dakota Johnson on ‘Saturday Night Live’; 'Verity' star calls the 'Patient Zero' singer her 'literal therapist!'
articles.summary: Dakota Johnson was halfway through a joke about her dating life when the camera cut to Taylor Swift.
articles.body: Dakota Johnson was halfway through a joke about her dating life when the camera cut to Taylor Swift. The singer had quietly appeared on the ‘Saturday Night Live’ stage during Johnson’s opening monologue on October 3, 2026, turning what started as a joke about famous exes into one of the night’s biggest surprises.Johnson, hosting ‘SNL’ for the third time, joked that since the previous appearance she had gone through “two very public, very lame breakups with two very awesome musicians.” She then talked about having friends who support her dating choices without judging her.That was when Swift walked out. “My literal therapist!” Johnson said, introducing her. Swift immediately played along.“I’m not your therapist. Actually, you just show up once a week at my house with an empty bottle of wine and ask if I want some,” she told Johnson. “Yeah, well, I have manners,” Johnson replied.Swift was not done. She joked that Johnson would “flop on my couch and overshare,” while she would occasionally respond, “Damn, that’s crazy.”“Is that not a therapist?” Johnson asked. It was the kind of exchange that worked because neither woman seemed particularly interested in making it sound rehearsed.Dakota Johnson jokes about dating musiciansJohnson kept the musician jokes coming. “I think actually I’m doing a public service by dating them,” she said, before claiming she was “saving you a lot of money on Zoloft.”“So, you’re welcome, America!” Johnson added, before expanding the joke to “England and parts of Ireland and Cleveland, allegedly.” Swift responded with a quick, “Woo-woo!”The Cleveland reference was not random. “Cleveland!” is one of the songs on Swift’s ‘The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore’, and the track includes references to her husband, Travis Kelce.Taylor Swift and Dakota Johnson reunite after ‘Patient Zero’The surprise ‘SNL’ appearance comes just days after Johnson appeared in Swift’s ‘Patient Zero’ music video alongside Colin Farrell. The video, directed by Swift, premiered during the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards on September 27, 2026. Paramount’s official announcement had confirmed Johnson and Farrell as the stars ahead of the premiere.Swift’s own website lists ‘Patient Zero’ among her directed projects, with Swift credited for direction. For Johnson, the ‘SNL’ episode also came at a busy time. She recently starred in ‘Verity’, and now she has another memorable moment tied to Swift — this time without a cemetery, a ghost story or a music video set.Just a couch, an imaginary therapy session and a very unexpected Taylor Swift cameo.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
