articles.title: Quote of the day by Hugh Jackman: ‘Work as hard as you can and make sure you have a good time while you're doing it,’ a powerful life lesson highlighting the importance of giving your 100 per cent
articles.summary: Explore Hugh Jackman's powerful life lesson on success and enjoyment. Discover why hard work and having fun are essential in pursuing your dreams and opportunities.
articles.body: A promotion, a dream job, a big opportunity, or simply being recognised for our work can start to feel like the moment when everything will finally fall into place. But Hugh Jackman seems to see success a little differently. For Jackman, it’s not just about where you end up. He has often talked about putting in the work, taking a chance when an opportunity comes along and enjoying the experience instead of always looking ahead to the next goal. His journey from Australian television and theatre to becoming a familiar face in Hollywood shows how much that mindset has shaped his career. Over the years, he has taken chances, welcomed new opportunities and made the most of every opportunity that came his way.Today’s quote of the day by Hugh Jackman reads: “Work as hard as you can and make sure you have a good time while you're doing it.”What does the quote by Hugh Jackman mean?Jackman shared the thought during a 2021 conversation with film journalist Jenny Cooney for the National Film and Sound Archive of Australia (NFSA). The interview explored his career, ambition and advice for Australians hoping to make it in Hollywood.While discussing ambition, Jackman said he never remembers having a specific dream of going to Hollywood, appearing in major films, hosting the Oscars or performing on Broadway. Instead, he recalled deciding that he would say yes to opportunities and work incredibly hard whenever he got a chance.“I thought to say yes, no matter how frightening it was, no matter how, even if you don't feel you deserve it yet or whatever, say yes, go for it, give it everything you have,” Jackman said. He then added, “Work as hard as you can and make sure you have a good time while you're doing it.”At its heart, the quote is about balance. Jackman is not suggesting that success comes without effort. The idea behind his message is pretty simple: work hard, but don’t forget to enjoy the work along the way. Things don’t always go according to plan, and an opportunity may take you somewhere you never expected. But being open to those experiences and putting genuine energy into what you do can make the journey feel just as meaningful as the result.Why Hugh Jackman’s quote still matters today?Jackman’s words hit differently today, when success is often judged by your salary, job title, followers or how many things you can add to your list of achievements. Putting in the effort matters, but finding some enjoyment in what you do matters too. When you actually like what you’re doing, the hard days can feel a little easier to handle. If you can find something you genuinely enjoy in the process, the hard work may feel a little less like a burden and a lot more worthwhile. For students starting their careers, professionals changing direction, or anyone pursuing a personal goal, the message is simple: take your opportunities seriously, put in the effort and do not forget to enjoy the experience.Jackman’s own career also gives the quote added meaning. During his NFSA interview, he described his approach as saying yes when opportunities appeared, even when they seemed frightening or he was unsure whether he was ready.That mindset can be useful beyond acting. Not every opportunity will lead to a breakthrough, and not every attempt will work out.Perhaps that is what makes Jackman’s words memorable. They are not simply about working harder. They areabout giving your best while still making room for enjoyment along the way.Hugh Jackman’s early lifeBorn in Sydney in 1968, Jackman initially studied communications at the University of Technology Sydney, graduating in 1991. He studied at the Actors’ Centre in Sydney and later attended the Western Australian Academy of Performing Arts (WAAPA), turning down an opportunity to join the television series ‘Neighbours’ so he could continue developing his acting skills.Jackman graduated from WAAPA in 1994. Around this period, he was still an aspiring actor finding his feet in the industry. The NFSA has preserved his 1994 graduation showreel, offering a glimpse of Jackman before international fame. A year later, he appeared as Gaston in a stage production of ‘Beauty and the Beast’.His early years were therefore less about instant stardom and more about training, performing and gradually building experience, a path that closely matches the idea behind his later advice about working hard and enjoying the process.Hugh Jackman’s rise to fameAfter graduating, Jackman began appearing in Australian television and theatre productions. He got one of his early TV breaks with ABC’s ‘Correlli’ and continued to build his career on stage, taking on roles in musical theatre as well. His stage career eventually took him to London's West End, where he made his debut in ‘Oklahoma!’ in 1998.His international breakthrough arrived in 2000 when he played Wolverine in ‘X-Men’.He went on to take on a wide range of roles, showing that there was much more to him as an actor than Wolverine. He went on to appear in movies including ‘The Prestige’, ‘Les Misérables’, ‘Australia’ and ‘The Greatest Showman’. At the same time, he continued returning to the stage, winning a Tony Award for his performance as Peter Allen in ‘The Boy from Oz’.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Actress Sshivada has wrapped dubbing for C Prem Kumar’s upcoming Tamil film, in which she is paired with Fahadh Faasil.
articles.body: Actress Sshivada has wrapped dubbing for C Prem Kumar’s upcoming Tamil film, in which she is paired with Fahadh Faasil. The actress says she was thrilled when the opportunity came her way, having admired the filmmaker’s work for years. “I was very excited. I had met him (Prem) a couple of times before this, but was always hesitant to ask for a chance. His films stand out and I love them as a viewer. His films connect well with the audience and, by the end of the day, there is always something to take away. It was his co-director Kannan who first called me for the film. My initial questions were all about whether I needed any preparation for the character. I said an immediate yes,” she states.'Prem sir gives an actor complete freedom'For Sshivada, the experience was memorable not just because of the film, but also because of the atmosphere on set. “What I particularly enjoyed was the way the entire team worked together. He is a great technician and a wonderful human being, and his rapport with everyone on set is lovely. He had come home to narrate the story while he was on his way back to Chennai. Apart from the film itself, the way he interacted with my family was special and made me feel comfortable immediately. He gives an actor complete freedom. If we do something good, he goes, ‘Wow, wow...’ and that is very rewarding as an actor.”'Fahadh improvises with every take'Sshivada plays Fahadh Faasil’s wife in the film and says she was impressed by the actor's approach to acting. She had first met him on the sets of Fazil’s Living Together. “After a few random meetings after that, we saw each other again only during this film's puja. Undoubtedly, he is a great actor and very nice to work with. What amazes me is that he improvises with every take and gives you something new. You can never guess what he is going to do next. It was wonderful sharing screen space with him, especially in a Prem Kumar project,” she says.'You will see a different Prem sir and Fahadh'While she is tight-lipped about the story, Sshivada stresses the film marks a departure from Prem Kumar’s earlier films, 96 and Meiyazhagan. “When I heard the script, I was expecting something like 96 or Meiyazhagan, but this is a completely different genre, packed with action — unlike the films Prem sir has done so far. You will see a different Prem sir in it. Even Fahadh is seen in a different avatar. I saw some of it during dubbing and I feel it has come out really well,” she shares.'All my Tamil film characters had something to explore'Sshivada also feels that Tamil cinema has given her more opportunities to explore different kinds of characters. “All my Tamil film characters had something to do, something to explore. I am not blaming anyone, but I have been typecast (in Malayalam) as the ideal person, a motivator, a good wife, etc. The one exception was probably Shikari Shambu towards the end. So, as of now, I am only listening to scripts in Malayalam and haven’t committed to anything yet. When I do a Malayalam film again, I would rather it be more of a comeback. And I look forward to that.” She adds, "In Tamil, the characters I am doing now and the ones I have lined up give me the chance to explore as an actress. I like seeing myself that way. As an actor, the Tamil industry is satisfying me more now."Apart from Prem Kumar's film, Sshivada has a Tamil web series awaiting release, in which she shares screen space with Sathyaraj, Bhagyaraj and Aishwarya Lekshmi. She has also done a guest role in Dharani Rajendran’s next and is currently shooting for Per Sollum Pillai, starring Kavin and directed by Ram Sangaiah.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: How authenticity is helping rooted stories break into the mainstream: Rasika Dugal, Amol Parashar, Mukesh Chhabra along with other industry voices share their perspective
articles.summary: Rooted stories are finding a wider audience as viewers increasingly embrace narratives grounded in specific cultures, communities and lived experiences.
articles.body: Rooted stories are finding a wider audience as viewers increasingly embrace narratives grounded in specific cultures, communities and lived experiences. The shift was discussed at a FICCI Frames panel featuring Mrinalini Jain, Tanya Bami, Amogh Dusad, Mukesh Chhabra, Anant Singh, Rasika Dugal and Amol Parashar, moderated by Naman Ramachandran. Producer Anant Singh said the focus should be on stories that mirror real life. “The point is to tell stories that aren’t being told, something that imitates life and is not filmy,” he said.Amol Parashar stressed that authenticity also requires commitment from actors. “As an actor, it is important to portray the right emotions and make the audience connect. It is easy to have six packs and look like Hrithik Roshan, but if you want to portray meaningful characters, those emotions and that commitment are required,” he said. Rasika Dugal spoke about choosing unconventional roles, citing Manto, Delhi Crime and Mirzapur. “The rewards are there to see,” she said, acknowledging that making such choices can be difficult.Casting director Mukesh Chhabra said the growing appetite for authentic stories has created space for new talent. “I am keen on finding real talent, good actors who can really act,” he said. The panel also discussed how rooted storytelling goes beyond small-town settings or regional dialects. What matters is whether the world feels authentic and the emotions connect. Mrinalini Jain noted that subtitles and dubbing have further expanded access to international content. “They are all rooted in their culture, but the emotion is universal,” she said. Parashar added that his mother’s interest in Korean shows illustrates the point: “They connect with the emotion and transport you to another world.”The discussion also highlighted several underexplored worlds, including family businesses, corporate boardrooms, children’s stories, women in comedy and the lives of entrepreneurs. The takeaway was clear: mainstream storytelling is no longer dependent on familiar settings. Stories that are specific to their worlds can travel when their emotions are universal.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Nabha Natesh is set to return to Kannada cinema with her next film, several years after making her debut in the industry.
articles.body: Nabha Natesh is set to return to Kannada cinema with her next film, several years after making her debut in the industry. The ‘iSmart Shankar’ actor is reportedly teaming up with Dhruva Sarja for an upcoming entertainer to be directed by Vishal Atreya, known for ‘Tatsama Tadbhava’. The project is expected to showcase Dhruva in a different avatar from his usual action-heavy roles.Nabha Natesh joins Dhruva Sarja for Vishal Atreya’s nextAccording to a report by Cinema Express, Nabha Natesh has been finalised for the yet-to-be-titled project, which will be directed by Vishal Atreya. The filmmaker made his directorial debut with ‘Tatsama Tadbhava’, which earned attention for its distinct storytelling. The upcoming film is reportedly being planned as a complete entertainer, with the makers keen to explore a lighter and different side of Dhruva Sarja.The collaboration will also mark Nabha’s first on-screen pairing with Dhruva. The actress has previously expressed her desire to return to Kannada cinema and was reportedly looking for a script that offered her something exciting. Vishal’s story is said to have impressed her and convinced her to come on board.Nabha Natesh to reunite with Kannada cinemaThe upcoming film is reportedly being produced by TG Vishwa Prasad under the People Media Factory banner. The makers are currently working on finalising the remaining cast and technical team. An official announcement is expected to be made as a special birthday announcement for Dhruva Sarja. Further details about the plot, characters and production schedule are likely to be revealed once the project is formally announced.Nabha Natesh’s journey from Kannada cinema to Telugu filmsNabha began her acting career in Kannada cinema with the 2015 film ‘Vajrakaya’, in which she starred opposite Shivarajkumar. Directed by A Harsha, the film brought her considerable recognition and earned her the popular nickname “Pataka Hudugi”. She subsequently appeared in the action thriller ‘Lee’ before moving into Telugu cinema.The actress made her Telugu debut with ‘Nannu Dochukunduvate’ and went on to gain wider recognition with Puri Jagannadh’s ‘iSmart Shankar’. Her return to Kannada cinema with Dhruva Sarja is therefore a significant addition to her career, particularly as she teams up with a filmmaker looking to explore a different space for the actor.Dhruva Sarja’s upcoming projectsDhruva Sarja was seen in ‘KD: The Devil’, in which he played the lead. articles.title: Kerala artist Joy Mathew’s works featured at Busan environment art festival
articles.summary: Contemporary artist Joy Mathew from Thrissur is among more than 800 artists participating in the Busan International Environment Art Festival (BIEAF),
articles.body: Contemporary artist Joy Mathew from Thrissur is among more than 800 artists participating in the Busan International Environment Art Festival (BIEAF), with both his works selected for its online exhibition, which began in September, and will continue until February 2027.“It’s very exciting to share space on a global stage with artists from different places. Both the works I submitted were selected,” says JoyKnown for his distinctive rock-art technique, Joy creates textured surfaces that resemble rock. “Most of my works follow this style, which has become my distinctive identity. I experimented a lot before arriving at it. Not every subject can be expressed through this technique, so it depends on what we want to convey,” he says.One of the selected works, Existence, explores resilience amid harsh living conditions. The painting depicts women and children making their way along thorny, pebbled paths under the scorching sun, with bamboo groves serving as a metaphor for resilience and community. “No matter which path they choose, only resilience can get them there. The bamboo is a testimony to this. But it also teaches us that growing aggressively does not have to mean suppressing others, because each bamboo knows that together they are a formidable force — a lesson in resilience and community,” he says.His second work reflects on the purity of the human heart in a world that has endured the fossil-fuel era, while looking towards technology and sustainable governance with hope.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Juventus wants to bring Miguel Gutierrez back to Serie A
articles.summary: Miguel Gutierrez was a key player for Napoli last season, but the club sold him to Bayer Leverkusen during the summer. He has made a strong start in Germany,...
articles.body:
Miguel Gutierrez was a key player for Napoli last season, but the club sold him to Bayer Leverkusen during the summer. He has made a strong start in Germany, which is why Juventus has been linked with a move for the defender.

The 25 year old was developed by Real Madrid and has enjoyed a fine career as a left back so far. Juventus believes he could perform well if he were added to the squad, with the club continuing to search for new players in that position.

The Bianconeri view Gutierrez as the perfect left back to sign as they look to strengthen the role. Calciomercato reports that Juventus intends to bring the defender back to Serie A.

The decision makers at the Allianz Stadium have worked hard to ensure that the team is in good shape to serve Luciano Spalletti and help him achieve success. Gutierrez is one of the left backs on Juventus's radar, according to the report.

By the end of the season, Juventus is expected to step up its interest in adding Gutierrez to the squad. The defender could also be open to the move, giving the club confidence that he would want to join and continue his career in Serie A.

Juventus has other left backs on its radar, but, as things stand, the club will likely make a move for Gutierrez next summer if he continues to perform well.

Gutierrez's form in Germany has increased the likelihood of interest from Juventus. The club reportedly believes that his experience as a left back would make him a suitable option as it considers changes to the squad.

Although Juventus is monitoring several players for the position, Gutierrez appears to be among its leading options. His potential willingness to return to Italy could also make negotiations more straightforward.

For now, Juventus will continue to watch his progress at Bayer Leverkusen. If he maintains his current level of performance throughout the season, the Bianconeri could intensify its efforts to secure his signature during the summer transfer window.

articles.title: Yami Gautam raises concern over AI-edited celebrity photos, urges media to 'use images in their original form': 'Altering or manipulating an individual’s image or likeness should not be done without their knowledge and consent'
articles.summary: National Award-winning actor Yami Gautam has urged the media and the public to refrain from using artificial intelligence to alter or enhance photographs
articles.body: National Award-winning actor Yami Gautam has urged the media and the public to refrain from using artificial intelligence to alter or enhance photographs of her taken during public appearances. Stressing the importance of consent, the actor said images featuring an individual should not be manipulated using AI without their knowledge or permission. Her comments come amid growing concerns over the misuse of AI to digitally alter celebrity images.Yami Gautam asks media not to alter her photos using AITaking to X (previously Twitter), Yami Gautam made a “sincere request” to the media, asking publications and photographers to use her photographs in their original form. The actor specifically objected to the use of AI tools to alter or enhance her appearance without her consent.Yami wrote, “A sincere request to the media. Please refrain from using AI to alter or enhance my photographs from public appearances. Kindly use images in their original form. Altering or manipulating an individual’s image or likeness using AI should not be done without their knowledge and consent. Thank you in advance for respecting my request!”Yami Gautam’s appeal comes amid growing concerns over AI misuseYami’s statement comes shortly after the controversy surrounding an AI-manipulated video involving Jr NTR and Janhvi Kapoor from their ‘Chuttamalle’ song in ‘Devara: Part 1’. The digitally altered content drew strong condemnation from Jr NTR, who warned that legal action would be taken against those responsible for creating and circulating it.Vijay Deverakonda and Chiranjeevi also expressed their support for action against the misuse of AI. Chiranjeevi called for stronger mechanisms to help those affected by such content, including greater coordination with cybercrime authorities and steps to facilitate the removal of manipulated material.Yami Gautam to play a supernatural character in ‘Nayyi Navelli’On the work front, Yami Gautam is set to headline ‘Nayyi Navelli’, a film that combines fantasy, family drama, dark humour and elements of Indian folklore. The trailer introduces her as Mohini, a model bride who enters a lively household in Meerut and initially wins over the family through her charm and culinary skills.The story subsequently takes a supernatural turn, with folklore and dark fantasy becoming central to the narrative. Yami is set to play a daayan in the film, marking a departure from several of her recent roles.‘Nayyi Navelli’ cast and crew‘Nayyi Navelli’ is directed by Balaji Mohan and written by Himanshu Sharma and Divy Nidhi Sharma. Aanand L Rai and Sharma are producing the film under the Colour Yellow banner, marking the production house’s first collaboration with Amazon MGM Studios.GV Prakash Kumar has composed the music for the project. The film is expected to bring together its supernatural premise with humour, family dynamics and elements drawn from Indian folklore.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
